motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single spatial easing: cue reveal, line swap, sheet slide, mic lift.

motion.name: cue-reveal
motion.purpose: Lettering written left to right across the band.

motion.name: line-swap
motion.value: top, height, font-size 0.45s var(--ease-out); opacity 0.3s ease
motion.purpose: A runner-up promoted to the top line.

motion.name: mic-lift
motion.value: transform 0.2s var(--ease-out), background 0.2s ease; hover translateY(-1px), active translateY(1px)

motion.name: bar-flash
motion.purpose: Confirmation that a sound started or changed at the bar.

motion.name: reveal-rewind
motion.value: 750ms easeOutExpo tween of the strip to 1.2 s before the take, with filter: blur(3px) on the strip
motion.purpose: The scripted whip back before the first detection of a take (JS, app.js).

motion.name: reveal-preroll
motion.value: 650ms hold, then 1.2 s linear tween into the bar
motion.purpose: The winner travels to the bar; the sound starts as it arrives (JS, app.js).

motion.name: strip-clock
motion.value: translate3d(-bandT * PPS px, 0, 0) each frame; PPS = max(90, bandWidth / 8.5)
motion.purpose: The band moves only with the take's currentTime.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition: none on .line, .cue, .sheet, .pic, .mic; animation: none on .bar.flash and .lamp; no whip blur; rewind and pre-roll skipped in JS
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce keeps the reveal without the travel.

narrative.overview:
A darkened dubbing auditorium. The screen is three stacked stage objects: a projected picture floating in a warm near-black room with a soft amber light spill behind it, a charcoal rythmo band with sprocket holes scrolling underneath it, and a hardware deck along the bottom. Nothing on screen is a web control dressed up; the mic is a drawn stage mic with a red lamp, the counter is a timecode readout, the inspector is a sheet of ruled paper that slides in from the right.

The band is the whole idea. Time runs horizontally at a fixed pixel rate; the matched sound arrives as marker lettering in Caveat, stretched to its real five-second duration, and the sound starts the instant the first letter crosses the one red-orange sync bar fixed at the band's centre. Density is low by design: the room watches from several metres, so there is one large line, three smaller lines, a bar, and a deck, and nothing else.

Motion belongs to the video clock. The band moves only when the take plays (plus one scripted rewind-and-write before each reveal); every other element is still, and state is shown by ink, lamp, and bar flash rather than by things moving around.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ground, paler charcoal strip, cream paper sheet: three materials, no greys for their own sake.
One accent (red-orange bar) that only ever means "sync": the bar itself, the recording lamp, focus rings, form accent colour, the sheet's margin line.
Five family inks with fixed meanings; white reserved for the playing cue.
Two faces: Caveat for anything written on the band, Atkinson Hyperlegible with tabular numerals for everything the deck and sheet say.
Container-relative band type (`cqh`) so the lettering scales with the band, not the viewport.
Flat surfaces; depth comes from the picture's projector shadow, the sheet's edge shadow, and the band's cut sprocket holes.

rules.name: The One Bar Rule
rules.body: Red-orange means sync or recording and nothing else. Do not use `bar` for emphasis, links, headings or decoration; on the sheet it appears only as the form `accent-color` and the margin line.

rules.name: The Fixed Ink Rule
rules.body: A family ink is bound to its family in every surface (band lines, sheet dots) and never reassigned for hierarchy, mood or state.

rules.name: The White Cue Rule
rules.body: Pure white is the playing cue's ink alone. Nothing else on the stage is `#ffffff`.

rules.name: The Band Is Caveat Rule
rules.body: Caveat is for things written on the band. The deck, the picture note and the sheet are Atkinson only.

rules.name: The Ruled Baseline Rule
rules.body: On the sheet, every line of text is 28px tall so it sits on the paper's rules; do not introduce line-heights that break the rule pitch.

rules.name: The Band Scales With Itself Rule
rules.body: Band lettering is sized in `cqh` against the band container, never in `px`, `rem` or viewport units.

rules.name: The Physical Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow exists only where a stage object would cast one: the projected picture, the paper sheet, the lit lamp, the flashing bar. No hover shadows, no card shadows, no ambient glows on controls.

rules.name: The Flash At The Bar Rule
rules.body: The bar flash is the feedback for a sound starting or changing. Do not add a second confirmation anywhere else.

dos: Do write anything that goes on the band in Caveat 600, sized in `cqh`, stretched to its duration with `scaleX` (max 2.4x) and finished with a rule to the cue's end.
Do keep the sync bar fixed at the band's horizontal centre and start or change sounds only there, with the bar flash as the confirmation.
Do bind colour to family through `data-family` and `--ink`, and render the playing cue in white.
Do set sheet text on the 28px rule pitch and use tabular numerals for every number on the deck and the sheet.
Do build controls as stage objects: outlined circles and rings on the deck, outlined paper buttons on the sheet, inline SVG drawn with `currentColor` or the mic's grey trio.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing travel and reveal animation while keeping the reveal itself (band in place, cues present, sound at the bar).
donts: Don't use `bar` for anything but sync, recording, focus and the sheet's form accent.
Don't reassign a family ink, use white for a runner-up, or tint the top line by family.
Don't move the strip with CSS transitions or on any clock other than the take's `currentTime` (plus the scripted rewind and pre-roll).
Don't put Caveat on the deck or the sheet, or Atkinson on the band.
Don't add shadows to controls, hover glows, or lifted cards; the only shadows are the picture's, the sheet's, the lamp's and the bar flash.
Don't size band type in `px`, `rem` or viewport units, or let the band row grow beyond its clamp.
